analysis.investment_thesis: Capri Global is a fast-scaling NBFC with a 37% revenue CAGR and 30% PAT CAGR over 9 years, riding the deeply underpenetrated Indian housing and MSME lending market — exactly the India financial inclusion story I love. However, a massive equity dilution in FY25 that doubled book value to INR 6,673 Cr, combined with ROE compressed to 11.8% and finance costs growing at nearly 68% CAGR, means the returns on that diluted capital base must be proven before this becomes a high-conviction buy.
key_strengths: Revenue grew from INR 189 Cr (FY16) to INR 3,248 Cr (FY25) — a 37% CAGR over 9 years — powered by home loans, MSME, and now gold loans; product diversification strengthens the franchise
Net profit of INR 479 Cr in FY25 represents 71.7% YoY growth, and forward P/E of 12.96x suggests the market expects strong FY26 earnings — valuation is not demanding relative to growth
Promoter holding at 59.92% with significant DII interest (20.09%) signals credible institutional confidence; business model is well-understood by long-only India funds
key_risks: Finance costs compounding at 67.9% CAGR — growing much faster than revenue (37%) — means net interest margins are being structurally compressed; any tightening in wholesale funding markets would hit earnings disproportionately

Total balance sheet assets grew from INR 7,153 Cr (FY22) to INR 24,413 Cr (FY25) in just 3 years — this pace of AUM growth in MSME and housing segments means credit quality hasn't been tested through a full cycle
ROE of 11.8% post-FY25 equity raise is below my 15% threshold; with equity now at INR 6,673 Cr, the company needs to deploy the capital profitably to earn back to 15%+ ROE — this will take 2–3 years
red_flags: OCF negative all 5 years (cumulatively -INR 13,078 Cr over FY21–25) — while normal for a growing NBFC, the scale of outflows means the business is entirely dependent on external capital markets; any funding disruption is existential
Total debt reached INR 15,577 Cr in FY25 against equity of INR 6,673 Cr — D/E of 2.33x is manageable for an NBFC but leaves thin buffer if NPA cycle turns adverse in housing or MSME

The large QIP/equity issuance in FY25 (equity base more than doubled from INR 3,837 Cr to INR 6,673 Cr) — significant dilution for existing shareholders; return on incremental equity must be watched closely in FY26 results
analysis.detailed_analysis: Capri Global operates in two of my favourite India structural themes — housing finance and MSME credit — where penetration is perhaps 15–20% of potential and the runway stretches decades. The 37% revenue CAGR over nine years is genuinely exceptional and the business model of originating secured, collateral-backed loans to underserved segments is sound. The FY25 results (PAT INR 479 Cr, +72% YoY; AUM scaling past INR 20,000 Cr) demonstrate that the platform is maturing. However, the massive capital raise in FY25 is a double-edged sword — it funds growth but compresses ROE to 11.8%, and I need to see this capital earn 18–20% returns before calling this a conviction buy. The near-68% CAGR in finance costs over 9 years — significantly outpacing revenue growth — suggests that spread economics need to improve as the book scales and vintage matures. I will wait for FY26 ROE recovery toward 14–16% and clearer evidence of asset quality stability before upgrading to a Buy.
